title: E5 reading checkpoint form A
instructions: Use an eighteen-minute rehearsal target: survey both passages, complete one passage before moving to the other, park an uncertain item after one focused attempt, and protect time to answer all five questions before submitting.

parts.prompt: Passage A: In paragraph 2, what does “That pattern” refer to?

options.text: The corridor dried quickly while water repeatedly remained beside the courtyard gate.
Leaves blocked the music-room drain on two of the three survey days in the first week.
Every wet surface on the grounds was equally dangerous after heavy rain.
The club photographed six fixed locations after rainfall.

choice_rationales.A: The phrase gathers the complete contrast immediately before it: the corridor improved, but water continued to collect at the gate.
choice_rationales.B: The blocked drain explains the first week's misleading result, but it is not the later pattern that moved the signs.
choice_rationales.D: This is a method detail, not the repeated result described by the reference expression.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: “That pattern” refers to the corridor drying while water continued to remain beside the courtyard gate after several storms.

parts.prompt: Passage A: What does “promising” most nearly mean in the final paragraph?

choice_rationales.A: Nara avoids a guarantee and calls for continued measurement.
choice_rationales.B: The reduction in pupils entering pooled water is useful enough to report.
choice_rationales.C: The results improved, but lighter storms prevent a certain causal conclusion.
choice_rationales.D: The club openly describes both the result and its limitation.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Promising describes evidence that is encouraging while still requiring caution and further confirmation.

parts.prompt: Passage B: In the final paragraph, what does “them” in “handing them over” refer to?

options.text: the people waiting for a meal

choice_rationales.A: The final paragraph concerns lending footwear, not delivering containers.
choice_rationales.B: The younger neighbour needs boots, and the narrator hands that plural object over.
choice_rationales.C: The marks are visible on the boots but cannot be handed over separately.
choice_rationales.D: The phrase refers to an object the neighbour can wear.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: “Them” refers to the red rain boots that the narrator lends to the younger neighbour.

parts.prompt: Passage B: What does “reluctant” most nearly mean in the opening sentence?

choice_rationales.A: This is the opposite of the narrator's opening attitude.
choice_rationales.B: The narrator can wear the boots but does not want to.
choice_rationales.C: The narrator complains and imagines being embarrassed, showing unwillingness.
choice_rationales.D: Gratitude develops only after the boots prove useful.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something.

parts.prompt: Which statement best identifies an idea developed in both passages?

options.text: A first impression becomes more reliable when it is tested against further evidence or experience.
Brightly coloured equipment always solves a safety problem, whatever the weather conditions.
Bad weather makes careful observation impossible, so first impressions cannot be checked.
Community projects succeed only when adults make every decision.

choice_rationales.A: The club revises its first map after more surveys, and the narrator revises an embarrassed judgment after using the boots.
choice_rationales.B: Neither passage makes a universal claim about colour or equipment.
choice_rationales.C: Rain creates the conditions in which both groups learn something useful.
choice_rationales.D: Young people observe, decide and act in both passages.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Both passages show an initial judgment being corrected or deepened through later evidence and experience.
